match.blurb: Match all the terms with their definitions as fast as you can.
match.rule: Match all the terms with their definitions as fast as you can. Avoid wrong matches, they add extra time!
howTo: You see 12 tiles: 6 terms and 6 definitions, shuffled.
Tap a tile, then tap the tile that goes with it.
A correct pair disappears; a wrong pair adds 1 second to your time.
The clock runs until every tile is gone. The lower your time, the better!
Keyboard: use 1–9, 0, - and = to pick tiles.

blocks.blurb: Place blocks, answer questions, and clear the board for a high score.
blocks.rule: Drag blocks onto the board and complete rows or columns. Out of blocks? Answer a question to get new ones!
howTo: Drag a block from the tray onto the 8×8 board. Each placed cell scores 1 point.
A full row or column clears for 10 points. Multiple lines at once and combos give a bonus.
When all three blocks are used you get a question. Correct: 3 new blocks. Wrong: one block fewer (minimum 1).
Use 'Refresh' to get a different card.
The game ends when no block fits anywhere.
blocks.answerForPieces: Answer the question to get new blocks
blocks.dragHint: Drag a block onto the board

blast.blurb: Compete to blast correct asteroids before time runs out.
blast.rule: Match definitions to the correct terms. Click or tap the correct asteroid to blast it with your ship before time runs out!
howTo: The prompt is shown at the top. Asteroids with possible answers drift below it.
Click or tap the asteroid with the correct answer: your ship turns and blasts it.
Each hit is worth 10 points × your streak multiplier. A miss resets your streak.
You have 8 seconds per prompt; the whole round lasts 90 seconds.
Keyboard: 1–5 pick the asteroid from left to right.
Pick your ship with the arrows before you start.

charms.blurb: Answer questions to earn moves, match colorful charms, and chase a high score.
charms.rule: Tap groups of 2 or more matching charms to clear them. Bigger groups score far more. Earn extra moves by answering questions correctly!
howTo: The board has 6 kinds of charms. Tap a group of 2 or more identical charms that touch.
Every tap uses 1 move. You start with 10 moves.
Group score = size² × 10. A group of 5 is worth 250 points!
Numbered charms are bonus charms: clear them and answer a question correctly to earn that many extra moves. Every third clear also triggers a question.
The game ends when you run out of moves or there are no groups left.

hangman.blurb: Guess the term letter by letter from its definition.
hangman.rule: Guess the term one letter at a time. You can make 7 wrong guesses before the drawing is complete!
howTo: You see the definition; the term is hidden behind dashes.
Tap a letter or type on your keyboard. Accents count as the same letter (é = e).
Every wrong letter adds a part to the drawing. After 7 mistakes the word is lost.
Fewer mistakes mean more points. A streak of solved words gives a bonus.
Stuck? Choose 'Give up' to reveal the term.

wordsearch.blurb: Find the terms hidden in the letter grid using the definitions as clues.
wordsearch.rule: Find the terms hidden in the grid. The definitions are your clues. Drag across the letters to mark a word.
howTo: On the right (or below) are the definitions. Each one belongs to a term hidden in the grid.
Words run horizontally, vertically or diagonally, also backwards.
Drag with your finger or mouse from the first to the last letter.
Found words stay highlighted. Turn on 'Show terms' if it gets too hard.
Find all the words as fast as you can!
wordsearch.skippedWords: {{count}} terms did not fit in the grid

speedreview.blurb: Rapid-fire multiple choice against the clock. Faster answers score more.
speedreview.rule: Answer multiple-choice questions against the clock. You get 5 seconds per question; the faster you answer, the more points you earn!
howTo: Every question has 4 answers and a bar that drains in 5 seconds.
A quick answer earns up to 100 points, a slow one at least 20. Wrong or too late = 0.
A streak of correct answers adds up to 50 bonus points per question.
Keyboard: 1, 2, 3 and 4 pick an answer.
After 20 questions (or the whole set) you see which terms you missed.
